calibrated_on: ubuntu-latest (GitHub Actions), Ruby 4.0.7, rbs 4.2.0, release-gate-frozen-corpus @ run 39187976225
note: Linux CI measurements of the v0.4.5 engine (a branch cut at the tag) over the frozen corpus v0.4.5: the tree at that tag, unpacked with git archive (#1507). allocations is the tight signal; wall_s is a coarse backstop. bench/README.md lists what the corpus run does not reproduce: gems' own sig/, the core RBS and Ruby, which come from the run, and a user-global BUNDLE_PATH. Advanced from corpus v0.4.4 after the v0.4.5 release (2026-10-19). The previous baseline (run 38915714928, the v0.4.4 engine on corpus v0.4.4) read 56,419,583 allocations, wall_s 67.907, peak_rss_kb 546,528. The v0.4.5 release candidate (run 39185243573, release/0.4.5 @ 48d8d94a5) passed on corpus v0.4.4 at 56,863,757 allocations (+0.79%), wall_s 73.919, peak_rss_kb 573,688. An earlier candidate run (39168858634) had failed on allocations at +3.4%: per-PR attribution named #2051 the largest share (+618,524 of the +1,893,302 rise): it amplified a subclass-map rebuild on every ivar proof that predates it. #2146 (subclass-map memo), which landed in this release, removed that rebuild and brought allocations back inside the band without re-baselining. This run (39187976225) reads 59,515,347 allocations, wall_s 56.472, peak_rss_kb 575,716. The engine measured is byte-identical to the release candidate's (lib, sig, data, plugins and Gemfile.lock are unchanged from 48d8d94a5 to the tag), so the move of +2,651,590 allocations (+4.66%) over that candidate is corpus growth alone: lib grew from 587 to 598 files with the v0.4.5 changes. wall_s is lower than the candidate's on a different runner draw; it is noise, not an improvement. The band is a budget for the engine cost added since this calibration. Refresh on the same corpus after an engine improvement by measuring the improving PR's own merge commit, and list in the new note every per-PR warning since this calibration with its answer; an unanswered one needs the user's ruling first. A red cut clears only by attributing the rise and recalibrating on the same corpus on the user's ruling. After each release the corpus advances to the new tag. bench/README.md and the rigor-release-prep skill carry the procedures. Sampling rule (#987): each gate run takes 2 reps per target, EACH IN A FRESH PROCESS (VmHWM is a per-process high-water mark, so an in-process rep can never report lower RSS, and a warm rep's wall is not comparable with this cold baseline), and records the LOWER of the reps for wall_s and peak_rss_kb while allocations and diagnostics are taken from the first rep unreduced. Measure a recalibration the same way -- bench/baseline.updated.json is already reduced, so committing it preserves the rule.
